purpose: Machine-readable source map for the Blackwell warp-specialization study. It connects every teaching claim and compiler-pipeline checkpoint to frozen source symbols, tests, and case-matrix entries.

evidence_kind.fact_with_scoped_inference: The mechanism and observed boundary are directly sourced, while the stated consequence is explicitly limited to the named input domain and does not claim runtime reproduction.

knowledge_points.title: NVWS is a two-epoch transient transaction dialect, not a direct LLVM input

evidence_vector.pipeline_or_api: direct AutomaticWS subpass order and dialect definitions
evidence_vector.focused_tests: parser/verifier, stage-phase, ARef lowering, warp-group lowering, and downstream conversion fixtures
evidence_vector.composed_or_target: ARef exits through TTG/TTNG barrier/TMA/TCGen5 ops; warp_group exits through ttg.warp_specialize
evidence_vector.runtime: not applicable to the transient-IR contract

knowledge_points.summary: NVWS defines two types, dialect attributes/interfaces, and 16 operations in four families. Current AutomaticWS first creates and fully consumes ARef plus destination-descriptor operations; only afterwards PartitionLoops creates nvws.warp_group, which LowerWarpGroup consumes into final TTGIR. The legacy tensor<Nx!nvws.token> channel is a distinct older path. NVWS has no direct LLVM conversion, so every normal path must eliminate its transient operations before target lowering. This is a normal-pipeline invariant rather than dialect-wide legality proof: verifier-accepted hand-written shapes can exceed the assumptions of greedy lowering.

sources.role: ARef, warp-group, legacy-token, and destination-descriptor definitions.
Proves the ordering of the two transient epochs.
Consumes ARef/descriptor families into buffers, barriers, TMA, fences, and TCGen5 completion.
Consumes the warp-group family into final TTGIR.

tests.checks: Positive round-trip coverage for part of ARef, warp-group, and legacy-token syntax, including a zero-region/no-result warp group; not a complete 16-op inventory test.

Depth, ordinary direct-user, enter arity, rank, shape, and type rejection; not unique-owner, zero-backing, exit-pairing, ArefBuffer result/token contracts, or complete warp-group terminator-domain coverage.
ARef/descriptor elimination into empty/full barrier, TMA, fence, and completion structures.
Default selection, worker-only form, and tensor capture lowering.
Final TTGIR WS control flow after NVWS has disappeared.

limitations: LowerAref and LowerWarpGroup use greedy rewriting rather than a dialect-wide ConversionTarget that proves all NVWS operations illegal at pass exit. The composite AutomaticWS CLEAN prefix rejects partition metadata/tag residue, not nvws.*; NVWS elimination is supported by source, local pass-trace observations, and focused lowering checks.

ArefCreate accepts variadic memdesc operands and its verifier does not enforce non-empty or unique ownership; exit token/completion-array pairing and ArefBuffer token provenance, result arity, and exact result types are protocol invariants. LowerAref checks the materialized ArefBuffer view count only with a C++ assert.

WarpGroup verification accepts zero-region/no-result form and does not validate positive/power-of-two warp counts, yield/result type equality, or terminator placement outside a result-bearing first region, while lowering indexes the first group and silently replaces each worker terminator with warp_return.
Unsupported AsyncOp combinations and malformed ARef users still reach assert, unreachable, no-arrival/deadlock, or legal-residue boundaries.
Legacy token insertion has parser and old code-partition fixtures, but no independent focused test was found that checks the complete WSLowerToken erase path.

knowledge_points.title: Partition-aware software pipelining separates cross-stage latency from MMA self-latency

evidence_vector.pipeline_or_api: AssignLatencies and ScheduleLoops run before AutomaticWS, with ScheduleLoops repeated after partition materialization
evidence_vector.focused_tests: direct latency, schedule, lower-loop, and mixed AutomaticWS fixtures
evidence_vector.composed_or_target: mixed TMA plus ordinary async-copy fixture composes WS and SWP

knowledge_points.summary: A partition inherits only a projection of the original stage/cluster schedule. If its latency operations occupy at most one stage, the second scheduler normalizes it to a one-stage loop. tt.latency controls def-use stage distance; tt.self_latency controls whether LowerLoops creates an MMA completion barrier and wait. Accumulator RMW or cross-MMA cycles suppress MMA user pipelining, while an ordinary tt.load operand prevents the fully-WS self-latency-zero shortcut. Enclosing scf.for markers put nested reduction loops in the same WS latency scope.

sources.role: MMA latency, self-latency, nested scope, and cycle policy.
Consume self-latency into completion wait protocol.

tests.checks: Fully-WS, nested marker, RMW, and token-cycle decisions.
Nonzero self-latency lowers to wait_barrier while the accumulator flag preserves the selected recurrence policy.
Basic dependency scheduling keeps an unannotated load with its consumer; backwards_prop_existing directly protects an existing WS schedule from destructive same-stage normalization.
Mixed path keeps useful SWP while same-stage roles do not gain false pipeline stages.

limitations: self_latency is scheduler metadata, not a measured hardware latency.
The source still has a FIXME to assert that every latency operation in a projected WS schedule has a stage entry.

knowledge_points.title: PartitionScheduling turns dataflow roots into a fixed-point partition assignment

evidence_vector.focused_tests: graph, merge, negative, scaled, attention, and persistent fixtures
evidence_vector.runtime: not applicable to the policy contract

knowledge_points.summary: A graph is built over loop operations. Descriptor-load results and TMEM-load tensor results seed data partitions; when optional token results are materialized, TMEM load and TCGen5 MMA/scaled-MMA token outputs are also seeded. Descriptor stores are eligible STORE nodes that consume propagated data, not initial data roots. Merge constraints and heuristics run to a fixed point, partitions propagate, cheap/view operations may be duplicated, and temporary IDs are serialized. The token edge is dependency/mod-ref dataflow, not a hardware completion event.
limitations: Partition boundaries are policy, not ABI; heuristic changes can alter the exact number or membership of partitions.

knowledge_points.title: PartitionLoops materializes independent warp-group programs

evidence_vector.focused_tests: structural and unresolved-SSA fixtures

knowledge_points.summary: The pass recursively clones scf.for, scf.if, single-result tt.reduce, and regionless ordinary operations into nvws.warp_group regions, remaps loop-carried values and captures, and rejects unresolved cross-partition SSA dependencies. Other region-bearing operations and unsupported yield parents reach assert or fatal paths rather than a generic RegionBranch implementation.
limitations: Correctness depends on preceding ARef/TMEM-ARef passes eliminating non-representable cross-partition SSA edges.

Current generic-control-flow support is scoped to explicitly encoded for/if/single-result-reduce forms; scf.while, arbitrary region operations, and multi-result reduce lack graceful negative coverage.

knowledge_points.title: InsertAref makes producer-consumer hand-off explicit

evidence_vector.focused_tests: producer/consumer, fan-out, scalar, and control-flow fixtures

knowledge_points.summary: Cross-partition tensor, scalar, and shared-memory values are wrapped in ARef create/put/get protocol operations. Tensor-descriptor loads become NVWS descriptor loads writing ARef-owned shared storage. Consumer exits require a structural post-dominator, and their actual first/last-use boundaries are chosen in pipeline time from the coarse stage/cluster schedule rather than textual block order.

sources.role: Convert descriptor load to ARef-aware producer.

tests.checks: One value with register and shared uses.

limitations: ARef is an intermediate compiler protocol; its operation names are not stable runtime ABI.

The normal inserter creates non-empty backing and completion arrays with paired tokens, but the dialect verifier does not prove non-empty storage, unique ARef ownership, exit-token pairing, or ArefBuffer token provenance.

knowledge_points.title: InsertTmemAref tracks TMEM ownership over optional dependency-token DAGs and a no-token alloc fallback

evidence_vector.focused_tests: GEMM, attention, scaled, and double-buffer fixtures

knowledge_points.summary: The pass first exits safely when the function contains no tt.warp_specialize loop marker, then builds a TMEM access DAG, normally following optional dependency/mod-ref token use-def chains; TMEM allocation with a source and no token uses a direct single-user fallback edge. The tokens act like MemorySSA ownership edges across TMEM RAW, WAR, and lifetime transitions, not hardware completion events. The pass stores the last async kind separately for each PartitionId so nested paths cannot overwrite one another, inserts ownership ARefs and stage annotations, and contains a loop-scheduler workaround. Its assertion counts at most two distinct explicit partition IDs and tracks an unpartitioned root separately, but subsequent acquire/release logic is still written for a two-owner ping-pong graph.

sources.role: Defines optional TMEM dependency/mod-ref token inputs and outputs.
Optional token use-def traversal plus the alloc-with-source no-token fallback.
Separates the optional root owner from the at-most-two explicit PartitionId=(partition, wsTag) set.
Keep asynchronous completion kind partition-local across nested DAG traversal.
Repair schedule information around the transformed loop.

tests.checks: No WS loop marker causes a safe no-op before ordinary TMEM DAG assumptions are applied.

limitations: More than two explicit partition IDs assert. Although root plus two explicit owners passes that particular count assertion, the remaining lowering assumes only one other owner and has no positive or negative three-owner proof.
The no-marker early return is not a unified preflight for marked-but-unpartitioned or already-partitioned unsupported owner graphs.
Scaled TMEM flows have targeted single-depth handling rather than a general proof for arbitrary graphs.

knowledge_points.title: LowerAref turns ownership into empty/full barrier protocols and multibuffering

evidence_vector.focused_tests: barrier, fan-out, attention, and multibuffer fixtures

knowledge_points.summary: ARefs lower to barrier allocation, wait/arrive operations, concrete TMA loads, and shared/TMEM stage buffers. Only global-to-shared descriptor/TMA producer ARefs are expanded to numStages by this pass; generic cross-partition ARefs remain depth one, TMEM depth is decided by its access DAG, and TensorMemoryScalesEncoding stays depth one without a leading ring dimension. Compatible ARefs can be combined. Exit AsyncOp is an explicit completion contract whose supported producer, consumer, and release subsets are narrower than the enum.

sources.role: Stage buffers and reduce redundant protocols.

limitations: Source comments acknowledge that some generated synchronization can expose less-than-ideal parallelism; structural correctness does not imply optimal overlap.

Producer arrival counting accepts TC5MMA/TMALoad/NONE, consumer counting accepts TC5MMA/WGMMA/NONE, and reachable release lowering covers NONE/WGMMA arrival, TC5MMA commit, and TMA hardware arrival; other enum values are not a supported matrix.
Zero backing, empty completion arrays, or mismatched transaction tokens are not uniformly diagnosed and can reach indexing, unreachable, or no-arrival/deadlock boundaries in hand-written NVWS IR.

knowledge_points.title: LowerWarpGroup establishes the verifier-covered ttg.warp_specialize boundary

evidence_vector.focused_tests: default/worker region fixtures plus final-IR verifier negatives

knowledge_points.summary: nvws.warp_group regions become ttg.warp_specialize partitions. The first group becomes the default region only when its warp count equals the module default; otherwise an empty default is created. The final IR returns SSA values only from the default warp_yield; worker warp_return has no operands, and explicit warp_specialize operations cannot be nested.

sources.role: Construct the final TTGIR WS operation.
Defines the final concurrent-region result and terminator contract.
Rejects nested explicit warp-specialize operations and verifies region structure.

tests.checks: Nested final WS and malformed region contracts are rejected before LLVM lowering.

limitations: Worker-to-default payloads require storage/ownership protocols rather than worker-region SSA results in the final TTGIR contract.
The explicit IR/lowering boundary prohibits nested ttg.warp_specialize operations; this is distinct from an outer marked scf.for containing an inner loop analyzed in the same AutomaticWS scope.

The NVWS verifier accepts a zero-region/no-result warp_group, does not validate numWarps domain or yield/result types, and does not constrain terminator placement outside a result-bearing first region. LowerWarpGroup indexes numWarps[0] and replaces worker terminators without checking their original kind. A result-bearing group whose first warp count cannot form the default may remain as legal NVWS residue because greedy rewrite failure is not pass failure and no ConversionTarget proves dialect elimination.

knowledge_points.title: HoistTmemStore folds TMEM initialization and conditionally hoists persistent clears

evidence_vector.focused_tests: narrow safe-hoist fixture

knowledge_points.summary: The first rewrite can fold any initialization store whose source definition dominates the allocation, not only a literal zero. The narrower persistent MMAv5 path commonly handles a zero clear and hoists the initialized allocation only when useD=false plus matching execution/trip behavior or a proof that the loop executes at least once.
limitations: This is a narrow pattern optimization; failure to match should preserve correctness but can retain synchronization and clearing cost.

knowledge_points.title: OptimizePartitionWarps shrinks worker groups with target-specific heuristics

evidence_vector.focused_tests: warp minima and register-estimate fixtures

knowledge_points.summary: Each partition is extracted and relayouted at candidate warp counts. The estimate uses twice the largest tensor i32-register footprint, a 65536-register SM budget, minimum 2 warps for TMA loads, minimum 4 for TMEM operations, and target register requests of 88 with tensor computation or 24 otherwise.

sources.role: Isolate and recompile a partition at alternate warp counts.

limitations: The register estimate is not ptxas occupancy analysis and does not predict runtime speedup.
Exact worker counts may change when layouts or heuristics evolve.

knowledge_points.title: AllocateWarpGroups gives worker partitions physical warp IDs and register budgets

evidence_vector.focused_tests: padding, safety-minimum, ID, and register-budget fixtures
evidence_vector.runtime: requested registers are not runtime occupancy

knowledge_points.summary: All WS operations are padded to the kernel maximum number of extra four-warp groups. Larger groups receive lower IDs, total-num-warps is recorded, requested registers are rounded in eight-register units, and the remaining budget is assigned to the default region. Assert/print regions and any region under an instrumented compilation retain a minimum of 32 registers, coupling sanitizer/debug survivability to physical register allocation. Start IDs are assigned consecutively and are not made TMEM-aware.
limitations: The source retains a FIXME about four-warp alignment for TMEM-related allocation and has no TMEM-aware verifier or negative test for this property.
AutomaticWS commonly leaves existing TMEM roles at four or more warps, but the heuristic does not repair an explicit undersized partition and is not an alignment proof.

knowledge_points.title: ConvertWarpSpecializeToLLVM lowers WS to a persistent worker state machine

evidence_vector.focused_tests: state, capture, CFG, rematerialization, and register fixtures

knowledge_points.summary: Warp IDs split the default path from worker paths. Worker warp groups repeatedly read shared state, switch to a partition body, synchronize, and return to the switch loop until an exit state. Captures are packed through shared memory; relative warp IDs and NVVM setmaxregister operations are materialized.

sources.role: Shared-state switch loop, capture storage, and partition CFG.

tests.checks: Captures, relative IDs, and arbitrary control flow.

limitations: PTX and especially SASS spellings are toolchain-dependent; the stable claim is the LLVM/NVVM control-flow and intrinsic structure.

knowledge_points.title: WS consumes a finite named-barrier budget

evidence_vector.focused_tests: barrier rewrite fixture
evidence_vector.runtime: not applicable to the hard budget

knowledge_points.summary: NVIDIA lowering has 16 named-barrier IDs. ID 0 serves the default context and ID 1 the switch rendezvous; partition-local handles use partitionIdx + 2. A worker region with index at least 14 that needs such a handle receives a diagnostic. A single-warp participant can use warp sync instead of a CTA named barrier.

sources.role: Defines the 0/1 reservations, partitionIdx + 2 mapping, diagnostic, and one-warp sync lowering.
Walks default/worker regions and requests target-specific handles.

limitations: Complex kernels can fail or require partition merging before reaching this limit; the budget is a hard implementation constraint, not a performance guideline.

knowledge_points.title: Correctness requires separate proxy and TMEM dependency analyses

evidence_vector.focused_tests: proxy and TMEM overlap fixtures

knowledge_points.summary: ProxyFenceInsertion orders writes/reads crossing generic, async, TMA, TMEM, CTA, and cluster proxies. TMemBarrierInsertion separately analyzes overlap among TMEM alloc/load/store/MMA/copy accesses. These passes run before LLVM lowering.

tests.symbol: async, TMA, TMEM, cluster, and 2CTA fixtures

tests.checks: Required TMEM barrier placement and non-overlap cases.

limitations: ARef barriers express producer-consumer ownership; proxy/TMEM passes solve additional memory-model hazards and are not interchangeable with ARef synchronization.

FenceAsyncSharedOp covers generic/async memory-proxy ordering; it is not tcgen05.fence. The frozen tree and exact SM103 artifact omit the ISA-canonical tcgen05.fence::after_thread_sync between cross-role MMA completion synchronization and a subsequent tcgen05.ld.

knowledge_points.title: Blackwell MMA lowers through TCGen05 and TMEM

evidence_vector.focused_tests: ordinary/scaled MMA and TMEM conversion fixtures

knowledge_points.summary: MMAv5 conversion constructs TCGen05 instruction descriptors and emits ordinary or scaled MMA. An asynchronous op with completion barriers commits/arrives on those barriers, and SyncMMALowering realizes synchronous semantics with a private barrier plus immediate wait/invalidate. Completion is not the whole cross-thread contract: PTX ISA's canonical MMA-to-TMEM-load sequence additionally uses tcgen05.fence::after_thread_sync before the asynchronous tcgen05.ld. The frozen dialect/lowering/tests and exact SM103 artifact contain commit, mbarrier wait, tcgen05.ld, and wait::ld but omit that specialized fence. Accumulators and operand staging otherwise use TMEM allocation/load/store/copy operations lowered to tcgen05 forms.

sources.role: Defines synchronous versus asynchronous completion semantics.
Realizes synchronous semantics through a private barrier and immediate wait/invalidate.

tests.checks: TMEM allocation under WS and captures.

limitations: TCGen05 is the compute substrate, not by itself evidence of automatic warp specialization; the IR must also contain the WS structure.

The current conversion tests and lab manifest require MMA plus commit but do not assert tcgen05.fence. Compile/assembly success therefore does not qualify ISA-canonical cross-thread ordering or runtime correctness for the MMA-owner to TMEM-reader handoff.

knowledge_points.title: Scaled MMA/block-scale is wired into partitioning and TCGen05 lowering

evidence_vector.pipeline_or_api: tl.dot_scaled tutorial source plus conditional compiler path
evidence_vector.focused_tests: partition, scale ARef/TMEM, and conversion fixtures; async selection is directly sourced
evidence_vector.composed_or_target: direct FP8/FP4 block-scale target checks; no Python-to-TTGIR provenance

knowledge_points.summary: TCGen5MMAScaledOp has an optional accumulator dependency/mod-ref token; when materialized, result 0 seeds partition dataflow. Scale operands may arrive through TMA/TMEM. LowerAref keeps the op asynchronous only when both scale paths are pipelineable; otherwise synchronous semantics are preserved and SyncMMALowering realizes them with a private completion barrier plus immediate wait/invalidate. MMAv5 conversion emits FP8/FP4 block-scale descriptors and TCGen05 block-scale variants, which alone do not prove asynchronous overlap.

sources.role: Optional token and sync/async completion semantics.
Requires both scaled operands to be pipelineable before selecting asynchronous ARef consumption.
Synchronous semantic fallback via private mbarrier and immediate wait/invalidate.
Scale descriptor and scaled MMA lowering.
Frontend tl.dot_scaled example, not an autoWS proof by itself.

tests.checks: Partition assignment with register/TMA scale sources.

limitations: The optional dependency/mod-ref token is distinct from completion barrier/commit/wait semantics.
Focused tests cover selected layouts/types and descriptor scale paths; this is not evidence that every tl.dot_scaled combination auto-specializes or remains asynchronous.

knowledge_points.title: Two-CTA evidence is a bundle of separately tested compiler components

evidence_vector.pipeline_or_api: conditional multi-CTA paths and a separate manual Gluon tutorial
evidence_vector.focused_tests: cta_group::2 conversion, cluster analysis, allocator, and all-warps lowering are separately covered

knowledge_points.summary: Separate fixtures establish: TCGen05/TMEM cta_group::2 conversion; distributed multi-CTA/cross-CTA dependency analysis; two-slot cluster mbarrier allocation; and modulo-4 slot/parity initialization/use that includes all WS warps. Double slots alone are insufficient: lowering takes a common CTA snapshot with a barrier before loading the shared counter, derives slot=counter&1 and parity=counter>>1, and uses another barrier after updating the counter so all participating warps advance together. This source map does not identify a single SM103 input that traverses AutomaticWS and all of those components end to end.

sources.role: Allocate two cluster mbarrier slots and module attributes.
Initialization, modulo-4 parity protocol, and all-warp synchronization.

tests.checks: Cluster barrier lowering, relaxed form, and slot reuse inside WS.

limitations: Component-level compile evidence must not be described as one end-to-end 2CTA fixture.
It validates selected IR/PTX structures, not launch viability, cluster residency, numerical correctness, or speedup on an SM103 device.

evidence_vector.focused_tests: broad TTGIR and conversion fixture set
evidence_vector.composed_or_target: coverage depth differs by workload and same-name does not establish provenance

For persistent attention and grouped GEMM, checked-in Python sources and TTGIR fixtures occupy separate evidence slots unless an explicit generation command/hash connects them; the 2CTA entries are a focused component bundle, not one end-to-end case.

knowledge_points.title: Unsupported boundaries have four distinct protection levels

evidence_vector.pipeline_or_api: eligibility no-op, explicit verifier diagnostics, and downstream invariant failures are directly sourced
evidence_vector.focused_tests: strong for common no-op and verifier paths but incomplete at hard limits
evidence_vector.composed_or_target: not applicable to most failure contracts

knowledge_points.summary: The implementation cannot be described by one fallback rule. No eligible descriptor memory, a serialized graph with at most one partition, and a function with no WS marker are separate safe no-op paths; malformed explicit WS, TMEM subviews, and direct cross-partition SSA receive diagnostics or pass failure; excessive TMEM owner IDs, cross-partition cp.async, malformed NVWS lifecycle IR, and unmodeled region control flow still use assert, unreachable, fatal, residue, or potential no-arrival/deadlock paths; TMEM start-ID alignment and selected attribute/state boundaries remain source-level gaps without complete negative fixtures.

sources.role: Return before partition metadata mutation when no eligible memory role exists.
Require both the request marker and serialized partition metadata before Shared ARef mutation.
No-marker early return, TMEM subview diagnostic, and two-partition assertion.
Shows that non-empty/unique ARef ownership, transaction pairing, numWarps domain, and zero-region lowering safety are not a complete verifier contract.
Unsupported async kinds and malformed non-empty/pairing assumptions can reach unreachable, first-element indexing, or a wait without release arrival.
Zero-region indexing and legal-residue boundary in greedy lowering.
At-most-one-partition no-op, unsupported region operations, and direct-SSA failure behavior.
Graceful register-protocol omission and unresolved TMEM start-ID alignment.
i8 state-count diagnostic and sentinel boundary.

tests.checks: AutomaticWS leaves a marked loop without eligible descriptor memory unmaterialized.
PartitionScheduling does not serialize an MMA-only graph without an eligible memory root.
TMEM ARef no-op when the function has no WS loop marker.
Unsupported TMEM subview receives a pass diagnostic.
A serialized graph with one partition remains an ordinary scf.for.

limitations: No direct negative fixture was found for the exact named-barrier/state-count limits, TMEM start-ID alignment, zero-backing/empty-async/token-mismatch or ArefBuffer result-contract NVWS transactions, NVWS warp-group terminator placement, root-plus-two-explicit TMEM owners, scf.while, or multi-result reduce.

Assert/unreachable boundaries may abort an assertion-enabled compiler and are not graceful autotune fallback; malformed hand-written barrier protocols can also compile into a wait lacking a matching arrival, while a malformed worker terminator can be silently replaced during LowerWarpGroup.

knowledge_points.title: Use independent evidence axes, then state a scoped qualitative maturity verdict

evidence_vector.pipeline_or_api: frontend hint and default SM103 compiler path are directly present
evidence_vector.focused_tests: dense for partition, ownership, allocation, lowering, and selected workload shapes
evidence_vector.composed_or_target: canonical GEMM has the most connected structural evidence; attention/grouped provenance and 2CTA composition have explicit gaps
evidence_vector.runtime: no SM103 launch, numerical, profiling, or speedup result in this study

knowledge_points.summary: The frozen tree supplies independent evidence axes: public/input shape, automatic discovery, focused pass contracts, composed fixtures, target lowering, generality restrictions, and runtime qualification. Dense final-lowering tests cannot compensate for narrow eligibility; Python source cannot substitute for recorded Python-to-TTGIR provenance; compile-only structure cannot substitute for SM103 runtime. The scoped verdict is that explicit IR, persistent lowering, and physical allocation are highly integrated; canonical TMA GEMM has the most mature compile-time path; automatic policy remains loop-local and heuristic; scaled, 2CTA, attention, persistent, and grouped cases have layered but incomplete provenance; production runtime qualification remains experimental and unestablished in this study.
limitations: The qualitative verdict is scoped to the frozen source and named evidence axes; it is not an aggregate score or universal workload guarantee.
Do not translate any structural axis into a universal performance or stability guarantee.
Exact-SM103 SASS exists for the four lab variants; device launch, numerical checks, profiling, and runtime measurements remain deferred until suitable SM103 hardware is available.
